parsed_payload.reasoning: The parabola \(y^2=-6x\) satisfies \(4a=-6\), so \(a=-3/2\) and the focus is \(F=(-3/2,0)\). Since \(\overrightarrow{FM}=k\overrightarrow{FN}\), the points \(M,N,F\) are collinear; thus \(M,N\) are the two intersections of a focal chord. Write the line through \(F\) as \((x,y)=(-3/2,0)+r(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\). Substituting into the parabola gives \(r^2\sin^2\theta=-6(-3/2+r\cos\theta)=9-6r\cos\theta\), so \(r^2\sin^2\theta+6r\cos\theta-9=0\). For \(\sin\theta\ne0\), the roots \(r_1,r_2\) give the two points and \(|MN|=|r_1-r_2|\). From the quadratic, \((r_1-r_2)^2=(r_1+r_2)^2-4r_1r_2 = \frac{36\cos^2\theta}{\sin^4\theta}+\frac{36}{\sin^2\theta} = \frac{36}{\sin^4\theta}\). Therefore \(|MN|=6/\sin^2\theta\). This is minimized when \(\sin^2\theta=1\), yielding the vertical focal chord \(x=-3/2\), with points \((-3/2,3)\) and \((-3/2,-3)\). Hence the minimum is \(\boxed{6}\).
